hook: One layout of objects drawn twice, as gravity and as electric field, so you see both laws fall off as one over r squared and that the real difference is that charge has two signs.
outcome: Use Newton's law of gravitation and Coulomb's law to compare gravitational and electric fields and forces, explain why both fall off as one over r squared, and predict how the forces between real pairs change with distance
sources: NIST CODATA 2018 recommended values: G, k (from the vacuum permittivity), e, proton and electron mass, Bohr radius: https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Constants/
NASA Earth Fact Sheet: Earth mass 5.9722 x 10^24 kg, mean radius 6371.0 km: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html
NASA Moon Fact Sheet: Moon mass 0.07346 x 10^24 kg, mean Earth to Moon distance 384,400 km: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/moonfact.html
OpenStax, College Physics 2e, section 31.1: nucleus scale about 10^-15 m (CC BY 4.0): https://openstax.org/books/college-physics-2e/pages/31-1-nuclear-radioactivity

OpenStax, University Physics Volume 2, sections 5.4 and 5.6, and Volume 1, section 13.2: field line conventions and the inverse square spreading argument (CC BY 4.0): https://openstax.org/details/books/university-physics-volume-2
Every Real pairs force and ratio is computed live from the constants above and was checked in Python (2026-10-25)
Twin boards use invented board units with the constant set to 1 on both boards, so the two pictures can be compared directly
Boards, field lines, diagrams, plot and bars drawn in code
Narration generated with Qwen3-TTS (Apache 2.0), cloning a Google Gemini text-to-speech voice
